learning_outcomes.text: Teach design techniques and algorithms for solving real-life problems that arise frequently in computer applications.
Teach principles and techniques of computational complexity (worst-case and average-case behavior, space usage, and lower bounds on the complexity of a problem).
Introduce the areas of NP-completeness and parallel algorithms.
Develop skills on efficient algorithm design.
Critically respond on issues regarding the efficiency of a new algorithm answering questions such as: Is the new algorithm efficient? Is there a better design and/or implementation?
Always be able to answer questions such as: How can this be done efficiently?
Always be able to answer questions such as: What data structure would be useful here?
Always be able to answer questions such as: Which operations should we focus on analyzing this algorithm?
Analyze algorithms and prove their correctness.
Be aware of how an algorithm actually behaves on various inputs.
Search for, analysis and synthesis of data and information, with the use of the Algorithmic thinking.

teaching_methods: Use of projector and interactive board during lectures
Use of computers in laboratories for development and testing of programs
Course website maintenance (announcements and posting of teaching material like lecture slides and notes, programs)
Announcement of assessment marks via the e-course platform by UOI

assessment_methods.method: Laboratory exercises of program development and testing

assessment_rules: Students are evaluated based on a final examination, laboratory exercises of program development and testing, and take-home programming assignments. For laboratory exercises, evaluation is based on whether students managed to write and test correctly the requested programs within the given time. Assignments are marked based on their correctness and completeness. The evaluation procedure is accessible to students via the course website.
